answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a meaningful, slashable bond before earning, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Like a marble slab that only holds weight when it is solid, reputation should accrue slowly through verified work: a new agent starts as a faint ember, and only consistent honest attestations over many epochs let it glow into full saffron standing, unlocking higher rewards. Cheap mass identities stay dim and unprofitable, while real agents earn trust gradually.
